evidence: Within the assigned score-type/anchor check, source inspection and TOML parsing confirm 74 Functional binary criteria, 6 Polish binary criteria, 2 binary gate criteria and 6 Visual likert criteria. Each Visual block declares points=5 and describes every raw anchor 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 (frozen task/tests/scored/visual/judge.toml:18-104); visual/prompt.md:48-53 explicitly requires these five integer anchors, identifies the intended normalization, and rejects aesthetic-perfection or preferred-style demands. This follows workbook Quality Checks #41 (C42:D42), with the Internal Quality Checks E42 binary-plus-weights annotation interpreted by the frozen skill known-false-positive rule and references/quality-checks.md:168-170. The borderline binary presentation requirements are feature-existence/usability outcomes: monospaced editor, line numbers, syntax colouring and actual theme changes, rather than their craft (functional/judge.toml, cw_editor_monospace through cw_editor_syntax_colouring and cw_theme_actual_switch/cw_theme_work_preserved; public ui.md:5-9). Polish tests pane usability, labels, keyboard reachability, focus existence, actual library navigation and understandable surface roles (polish/judge.toml:18-68). workspace_organisation defines identifiable editor/output/saved-work roles, without a pane arrangement or aesthetic standard. Visual retains degree-of-quality judgments for typography, contrast, spacing, hierarchy, consistency and viewport composition. Adversarial source-level checks: a working app with frequent collisions or poor font choices retains its independently earned behavior results but falls to described Visual anchors 2-4, so a binary craft threshold cannot conceal these differences. A conforming simple/native implementation with readable mono editor, labelled conventional panes, native focus and a stacked mobile layout remains eligible for full credit: visual/judge.toml:25,40,55,70,85,99-100 and polish/judge.toml:23,50 expressly accept these alternatives. These are counterfactual rubric interpretations, not measured app grades. All 84 frozen task/rule files match the manifest hashes and assigned input ce4b8f85ae12d3b7c3fe222c948c79364600e082541c3b04f1a16039a553cea8. The raw index as read had SHA256 0ce9a42ec24081625d883e612da454dd619a63d492eec16f3af5588cd13b1cc6; all 527 indexed artifact hashes matched. That hash check establishes integrity only. The index expressly leaves full configured judge workload, Oracle grade, Luna score and empirical reward ordering unmeasured; none is inferred here. This Pass is limited to criterion type selection and complete written anchors, which are directly inspectable source properties, and does not clear separate runtime rows.
